text: The report hypothesizes that its +0.086 effect may represent the irreducible post-compensation cost of expressing a functional protein with no benefit without antibiotics.

heading: Literature Context

text: The report cites Roux et al. (2015) as showing that resistance genes, particularly efflux pumps, can be beneficial in vivo by exporting host antimicrobials.

heading: Literature Context

text: The report cautions that its in vitro resistance-cost measurement may overestimate the true ecological cost.

heading: Literature Context

text: The report interprets its consistent signal across 25 diverse organisms as suggesting robustness of resistance cost across genetic backgrounds despite epistasis.

heading: Literature Context

heading: Novel Contribution

text: Broad-spectrum resistance mechanisms show stronger antibiotic-dependent importance than narrow-spectrum mechanisms (MWU p = 0.007).

text: All 25 organisms in the AMR fitness-cost report are lab-adapted strains, so compensatory evolution during laboratory maintenance may cause natural-population costs to be underestimated.

text: 86% of AMR genes are Tier 2 keyword matches from bakta annotations that may include non-AMR genes such as general efflux transporters, although consistent Tier 1 sensitivity results mitigate this concern.
quote: 86% of AMR genes are Tier 2 (keyword-matched from bakta annotations), which may include some non-AMR genes (e.g., general efflux transporters). The Tier 1 sensitivity analysis shows consistent results, mitigating this concern.

text: Only 4 AMR classes—beta-lactam, aminoglycoside, chloramphenicol, and tetracycline—have matched antibiotic experiments in the report.

text: Macrolide, glycopeptide, and polymyxin resistance classes could not be validated against matched antibiotic experiments.
quote: Other classes (macrolide, glycopeptide, polymyxin) could not be validated.
heading: Limitations

text: ~4.6% of AMR genes are putatively essential because they are absent from fitness matrices, and the estimated +0.086 cost would be a lower bound if these are the most costly AMR genes.

text: RB-TnSeq measures fitness relative to the pool average rather than absolute fitness.
quote: RB-TnSeq measures fitness relative to the pool average.

text: The report's +0.086 effect is the difference between AMR knockout fitness (−0.024) and non-AMR knockout fitness (~−0.11), not an absolute selection coefficient.

text: Transposon insertions can cause polar effects on downstream genes, potentially confounding fitness measurements for AMR genes in operons.
quote: Insertions can cause polar effects on downstream genes, potentially confounding fitness measurements for AMR genes in operons.

text: The Tier 2 product classifier omits fosfomycin and tellurite resistance annotations, leaving ~25 genes in the unknown mechanism category that could be reclassified as enzymatic_inactivation and metal_resistance respectively.
